claims.text: Adding 1–2 wt% Si to Mo–Nb–Ta–W and applying the specified two-step heat treatment will form in situ silicide films at grain boundaries.
The resulting grain-boundary silicide films will be nanometer-thin and well distributed.
Homogenization at 1200 °C followed by heat treatment at 700–800 °C will promote formation of the silicide films.
The silicide films will stabilize the grain boundaries.
The silicide films will impede grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature exposure.
The silicide films will impede grain-boundary migration during high-temperature exposure.
Suppressing grain-boundary sliding and migration will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Suppressing grain-boundary sliding and migration will improve creep resistance.
The Si-modified alloy will exhibit roughly a 30% improvement in high-temperature yield strength relative to the non-Si baseline.
The Si-modified alloy will exhibit roughly a 30% improvement in creep resistance relative to the non-Si baseline.
The predicted high-temperature improvement will occur at 900–1000 °C under tensile or sustained-load testing.
The Si addition and silicide-film formation will not significantly alter the overall alloy density.
The intervention will not degrade room-temperature ductility.
The modified alloy will retain comparable or slightly improved room-temperature strength.
The magnitude of improvement and the distribution of silicide films may vary with deviations in heat-treatment parameters.
Long-term stability of the proposed silicide films under prolonged service exposure has not been established.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as receiving only the conventional homogenization cycle, whereas the no-Si control in the experiment is said to receive identical overall processing conditions, which could include the additional 700–800 °C treatment. These are different controls and could produce different comparisons.
